title: Building a Generous Society and Nation
what_it_is: Building a Generous Society and Nation

sections.label: CDC vouchers and charity donations
sections.summary: The 2024 CDC vouchers will help offset higher living expenses, and the option to donate them to charity is applauded.

sentences.speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The most recent distribution of Community Development Council (CDC) vouchers for 2024 will certainly be welcome for many to help offset higher living expenses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I would also applaud the Government's initiative to offer the option to households to donate CDC vouchers to charity.

sections.label: Nurturing grassroots philanthropy
sections.summary: Live charity shows bring society together in giving, and the speaker proposes nurturing grassroots philanthropy to its fullest potential.

sentences.speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: If you look over the years, you would find that our live charity shows, for example, bring together wide sections of our society in generous and spontaneous giving.

sentences.speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I propose we take on the task of nurturing grassroots philanthropy and building generosity to its fullest potential.

sections.label: 12-year-old raises $1.2 million
sections.summary: A recent report featured 12-year-old Ms Chng Rui Jue, who has raised over $1.2 million for charitable causes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Another recent report featured 12-year-old, Ms Chng Rui Jue, who has raised over $1.2 million for charitable causes.

sections.label: Singapore's World Giving Index rank
sections.summary: The Charities Aid Foundation's 2023 report ranks Singapore 22nd out of 140 countries in its annual World Giving Index.

sentences.speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In its 2023 report, the Charities Aid Foundation that does an annual World Giving Index ranks Singapore as 22nd out of 140 countries.

sections.label: Longer tax incentive for IPCs
sections.summary: The speaker appealed for the 2.5 times tax incentive to IPCs to run longer than three-year cycles, such as five years or more.

sentences.speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Attracting both the financial resources and the service providers to work out local, regional and global solutions is such a powerful and impactful combination.

sentences.speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I had made an appeal for the 2.5 times tax incentive to IPCs to be made available for longer than three year cycles, to enable longer-term planning in both giving and in receiving.

sentences.speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Providing, for example, a five year or longer, rolling cycle would enable both the donors and the beneficiaries to enhance planning of services with greater certainty.

sections.label: Internationalisation support for social service agencies
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether a suitable internationalisation support programme could be looked at for suitable social service agencies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Just as our social entrepreneurs look to scale their programmes outside of Singapore, could we look at a suitable support programme for internationalisation for suitable social service agencies.

sections.label: Care needs and funding balance
sections.summary: Care for groups with special needs can require high staffing ratios, and funding initiatives must be balanced so they are not solely donor driven.

sentences.speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: For instance, the care of certain groups with special needs can require a high ratio, even one-to-one staffing such as adults with autism in a care facility.

sentences.speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: When it comes to identifying needs in the community and allocation of resources, we also need to keep the right balance so that the funding of initiatives does not result in solely being donor driven.

sections.label: Online giving during COVID-19
sections.summary: During COVID-19, online giving benefited and replaced more traditional platforms.

sentences.speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: During COVID-19, we saw how online giving benefited and replaced more traditional platforms.

sections.label: Hope for a generous Singapore
sections.summary: The speaker hopes Singapore will one day be recognised not just as an economic miracle but as a generous society and nation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As we continue to unite and persevere in our shared aspirations, I believe that one day, hopefully in the not too distant future, Singapore will not just be recognised as an economic miracle but, also, as a generous society and a generous nation contributing toward a better world.

sections.label: Volunteer Centres recruit 100,000 volunteers
sections.summary: Over the past five years, Volunteer Centres have recruited, trained and deployed over 100,000 volunteers to meet ground needs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: Over the past five years, Volunteer Centres have recruited, trained and deployed over 100,000 volunteers to meet ground needs.

sections.label: Enhanced Corporate Volunteer Scheme tax deduction
sections.summary: From 1 January 2024, the enhanced Corporate Volunteer Scheme allows businesses a 250% tax deduction when employees volunteer or are seconded to an IPC.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: The enhanced Corporate Volunteer Scheme, which came into effect this year, 1 January 2024, allows businesses to claim a 250% tax deduction when their employees volunteer or are seconded to work at an IPC.

sections.label: PAA pledges and FAST-P green finance
sections.summary: PAA has over 80 members and partners with $1 billion in pledges, and Singapore announced FAST-P, aiming to mobilise up to US$5 billion for green projects.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: PAA has now over 80 members and partners globally, with collective pledges of $1 billion.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: At the 28th United Nations Climate Change Conference, Singapore also announced new initiatives to catalyse a green transition here in Singapore and also beyond our shores.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: This includes the Financing Asia's Transition Partnership (FAST-P), a blended finance initiative that aims to mobilise up to US$5 billion to de-risk and finance green and transition projects in the region by bringing together partners from the public, private and philanthropic sectors.

sections.label: Tax deduction for donations
sections.summary: The Ministry of Finance extended the 250% tax deduction rate for qualifying donations to IPCs and eligible institutions until end 2026, and will review a sustainable level.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: The Ministry of Finance recently extended the 250% tax deduction rate for qualifying donations made to IPCs and eligible institutions for three years until end 2026.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: This tax deduction rate is high compared to other jurisdictions and we will review what a more sustainable level of tax deduction should be for the longer term while balancing support for our local charity sector.

sections.label: CFS new donor programme
sections.summary: CFS is working with the Ministry of Social and Family Development and Community Chest to introduce a programme connecting donors to needs on the ground.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: Meanwhile, CFS is working with the Ministry of Social and Family Development and Community Chest to introduce a new programme that better connects donors to the needs on the ground.

sections.label: Joining SG Cares Movement
sections.summary: People can join a local SG Cares Movement by signing up with their nearest Volunteer Centre.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: Join a local SG Cares Movement by signing up with your nearest Volunteer Centre today.
